warnings: Repeated checkpoints, alignments and chronology copies are dependent; they do not increase the independent election count. Same-day regular/special races are distinct contests in a shared state/election cluster; the legacy independent_contests field counts distinct contests, not independent voters or independent national environments.
County historical party margin is ecological context, not a current voter’s candidate choice.

The frozen 0.35 coefficient was not learned from these outcomes or preregistered before those elections. This retrospective algorithm audit can expose errors but does not prove prospective generalization.
Sparse historical EV coverage does not support calibrated probabilities, Brier/log-loss scores or 80%/95% EV interval-coverage claims.
Same-stage calendar days do not establish equivalent voting opportunities or unchanged pandemic-era voting rules.
Original contemporary final-result publication timestamps are not fully archived; final labels are actual later certified/compiled returns.
Present-day source-quality quarantines clean the evaluation universe; strict-contemporary denotes eligible feature-publication chronology, not a fully archived historical production system.
Experimental conditional party-margin research calls; not validated EV forecasts or winner probabilities.
Actual EV-assumption backtests are separate from historical-reference validation. Sparse independent evidence has not established a transferable learned conversion or calibrated probabilities.
The official 2026 ballot/candidate roster is not yet verified in this local dataset. Party labels do not certify candidate identities.

historical_reference.description: Recency-weighted historical Senate R-minus-D margin; different seats/candidates and election environments can make this a weak current-race reference.

geographic_tilt.description: Current county shares versus compatible same-stage historical early-vote shares. Each share difference is weighted by that county’s historical R-minus-D margin. It does not reveal how current early voters voted.
geographic_tilt.boundary_assumption: Canonical current reporting-county IDs are associated with their historical context; no votes are allocated across boundaries. Current-vintage continuity is a modeling assumption, not a verified precinct crosswalk.
geographic_tilt.same_stage_explanation: Same election type and days until Election Day, anchored to the latest actual current report. Historical dated-report evidence was available by the current research cutoff; it is not relabeled as contemporaneous historical validation.

turnout_projection.range_kind: Historical-analogue sensitivity span; no probability coverage.
turnout_projection.method: Current same-stage EV divided by the median prior same-election-type stage-EV/final-participation fraction. No candidate vote, target final total or target final registration enters the predictor.
turnout_projection.reason: Explicit prior-cycle participation analogue. Changes in voting modes, rules, reporting and final EV share can make this extrapolation wrong.
turnout_projection.chronology: Current contemporary observations with explicitly retrospective historical analogues.

explanation: The historical Senate reference is +3.3 percentage points Republican minus Democratic, built from 2022, 2020, 2016.
County EV geography shifts the research point by -1.0 pp (raw geographic tilt -3.0 pp × 0.35, capped at ±5 pp).
assumptions: This is a party-margin research projection, not observed candidate votes, a certified result, or a validated winner probability.

The reference pools different Senate seats, candidates and classes. It is not nominee-adjusted; current ballot identities and incumbency are unverified and no historical candidate is assumed to be running.

Historical reference: up to three most recent Senate-election years within 12 years, with a six-year recency half-life. Contests in the same state/year receive equal weight; unrelated candidate votes are never added.
EV adjustment = 0.35 × the change in county-weighted historical party margin, capped at ±5 percentage points. Both the coefficient and cap are unvalidated research assumptions.
Current early voters and later Election Day voters can differ sharply. Individual early-voter choice is unobserved; county correlations do not identify it.
The reported range is a deliberately wide, unvalidated sensitivity range, not an 80% or 95% confidence/credible interval.
Polling, party registration and demographic marginals do not enter this initial projection. No unreported age-by-party, religion, propensity or demographic intersections are manufactured.
warnings: Candidate configurations and survey populations are never pooled together.
Conflicting sources exist; configured source priority determines the displayed value.
Historical reconstruction exists; switch evidence mode to inspect its documented basis. It cannot establish what was reported then.
Matched geographies have asynchronous or unequally aligned report dates; inspect each place's source date before interpreting pace.
Records lacking contemporary publication evidence are excluded from this cutoff.
Survey response shares are preserved; undecideds are not reallocated.
Historical published candidate returns are election context, not early votes or contemporaneous reporting snapshots.
Margin is winner lead in percentage points; Democratic margin is D minus R; swing is change in D minus R.
Matching geographic identifiers do not establish identical boundaries across vintages.
Historical state Senate returns pool different seats, candidates and classes. Current nominees and incumbency are unverified; the projection is not candidate-adjusted.
